glass: cocktail glass (about 180 ml), chilled, no ice
version: v1.1 (Tomás, round 4 step 1, 2026-10-04; recipe unchanged from v1, round 2). Story: Charles K. Field's Hotaling verse on the 1906 fire and his anonymous Cheerio (Wren r1 accepted the plan's lead with conditions). A bourbon Martini: the whiskey is the punchline, 60 of the 90 ml poured in (about 46% of the finished drink after stirring), stirred and served up so nothing dresses it. Dry vermouth for the dry line (Codex p. 65: spirit plus aromatized wine), stirred. Spark: a spoon and a half of fresh pear syrup, made overnight, the sincere thing inside the dry drink (Flavor Matrix pdf 196: bourbon among the best pairings of the pear's family, the apple/pear/quince entry; scoped to the family, never 'pear and bourbon are a classic pair'). No pear on the glass, and no layer: it's stirred in, there in every sip if you look for it. The frame is a Manhattan made with dry vermouth, a nineteenth-century classic (Oxford MARTINI pdf 1244; Imbibe! pdf 194; date contested, so no year). Swept: bourbon 40-50%, vermouth 15-30 ml, pear syrup 5-10 ml at 50-70 g, acid 0-0.2%.

garnish.note: squeezed over the top, then taken away
